stage_a.note: Clear positive engagement recurs alongside substantial neutral stretches, especially when taking off their coats.
Sustained engagement with the subject is evident, shown energetically when removing their jackets.
Friendly, approachable and considerate expression characterizes much of the presentation as they smile at the panel.

venture.description: Single origin spices sourced directly from partner farmers worldwide, bypassing middlemen.
venture.note: The founders explain their direct sourcing model for single origin spices.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder introduces himself and the problem of flavorless supermarket spices.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Founder introduces himself and the company Burlap and Barrel.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder explains they are a single origin spice company working directly with farmers for better spices.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Founder describes their heirloom cinnamon from Vietnam and wild black peppercorns from Zanzibar.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder explains they bypass middlemen to pay farmers more and provide fresher, traceable, higher quality spices.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Founder states they are seeking 500,000 dollars for 5 percent equity in their company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder asks the panel if they are ready to spice things up in the kitchen.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder invites the panel to smell and taste the four best-selling spices provided to them.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder introduces the royal cinnamon from Vietnam, describing it as very rare, sweet, and spicy.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Investor notes the cinnamon tastes very different from conventional cinnamon.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Investor agrees the cinnamon is incomparable and really good.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Investor adds that the cinnamon is really good.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder introduces black lime from Guatemala, explaining it is sun-dried and ground into powder.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Investor suggests the black lime would be great in a marinade.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder agrees it is great in a marinade and has a distinctive flavor.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Investor remarks that the black lime is very unusual and they like it.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Founder introduces wild cumin hand-picked in the mountains of Afghanistan.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Investor comments on the strong flavor of the cumin.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder explains he lived in Afghanistan and this spice started the company.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Investor says they are not going to eat the peppercorn.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder encourages the investor to try the peppercorn, warning it is very hot.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Investor shares that they ate a peppercorn and found it excellent.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Investor asks how many individual spices they currently have in their portfolio.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder replies they have about 75 individual spices in their portfolio.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Investor asks if their sales are exclusively through online channels.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Founder clarifies they are 85 percent direct to consumer and 15 percent wholesale to restaurants and grocery.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Investor asks the founders to share their backgrounds and how they got into the spice business.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Founder explains they have been friends for 15 years, bonding over one cooking and the other eating.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder shares he left kitchens for graduate school and managed a large nonprofit in Afghanistan.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Investor asks what specific work the founder was doing in Afghanistan.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder details building over 200 schools and doing logistics for doctors without borders before discovering the cumin.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Founder adds that his co-founder is one of the foremost experts in spices globally.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Investor asks the founder to explain what happened after he found the cumin in Afghanistan.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder confirms he brought the cumin back to New York in a duffel bag.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Investor expresses surprise at the duffel bag detail.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder explains he shared the spice with restaurant friends, received overwhelming response, and started the business.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Investor asks if the business was initially run out of his New York apartment.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder confirms they ran the business from his living room for the first few years.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Investor asks for the business numbers, including costs, margins, and total sales.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Founder details their retail price, landed cost, 75 percent margin, and 12 million dollars in lifetime revenue.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Investor asks the founders to walk through their sales history over the past six years.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Founder states they generated 100,000 dollars in revenue during their first year.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Investor asks what calendar year that first year of sales was.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Founder lists sales growing from 2017 to 600,000 dollars by 2019.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Founder explains that during the 2020 pandemic, sales jumped to 3 million dollars.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Investor notes that a lot of people were cooking during that time.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Founder adds they closed 2021 with 5.1 million dollars in sales.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Investor asks what their projected sales are for the current year.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Founder states they are on track to do between 6 and 7 million dollars in revenue.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Investor congratulates them on their sales growth.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Investor asks what their projected profit will be on those sales.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Founder replies their net profit margin is around 10 percent.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Investor calculates and asks if that means 690,000 dollars in profit.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Founder confirms the profit figure is correct.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Investor praises their accomplishments but exits because he lacks knowledge about the spice business.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Investor compliments the taste but exits because she feels the spice market is too crowded.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Investor exits, stating the valuation is too high and she wishes they had asked for less money.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Investor praises the product quality but exits due to concerns about their ability to scale quickly enough.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Founder asks the remaining investor for his thoughts on a potential deal.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Investor expresses concern that the investment amount is too large to recoup easily and wants a multiple.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Founder states they came prepared with a specific deal idea for the investor.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Investor agrees to hear the founder's proposed idea.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Founder explains their strategy of doing collaboration blends with influencers for customer acquisition.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder adds that the 20 percent royalty on an 11.99 product equals 2.39 per unit sold.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Investor interrupts to offer 500,000 dollars for a 2.30 royalty on every order.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder clarifies they want to create a specific branded set of spices with the investor.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Investor notes that the founder's idea is a completely different deal structure.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Investor asks if the royalty would only apply to that specific branded product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder confirms the royalty would only be on the sales of that specific jar.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Investor clarifies that the royalty would not apply to all jars, just the new specialty one.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Investor withdraws his offer, stating he would never get his money back under those terms.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder argues that the investor's reasoning makes no sense.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Investor reiterates that the founder's proposed structure makes no sense to him.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Investor asks the remaining investor to clarify what his actual offer is.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Investor offers 500,000 dollars for 10 percent equity and a 20 percent royalty on everything until 1 million is recouped.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Founder counters with 5 percent equity, a 20 percent royalty on a branded line, and a 10 percent affiliate cut.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Investor rejects the counter offer and exits the negotiation.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Founders thank the panel for their time and feedback.

decisions.note: Not a business he knows anything about; ketchup is his ultimate spice.
Tastes great but it is a really crowded space; wants things more unique.
Valuation is crazy; wishes they had asked for $250,000.
Surprised she has never heard of the brand; doubts it can grow at the desired speed.

decisions.terms: $500,000 for a $2.30 royalty on an order
decisions.note: Wants a multiple of his money back on every order.
Refuses to do the deal if the royalty is only on a single specialty jar.

decisions.terms: $500,000 for 10% equity, and a 20% royalty on everything until $1 million is recouped
decisions.note: Offers a standard royalty deal to get his money back quickly.

decisions.terms: 5% equity for $500,000, 20% royalty on a Mr. Wonderful line, 10% affiliate cut
decisions.note: Counters with a targeted royalty and affiliate cut instead of a blanket royalty.
